title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up an abstract combinatorial structure on a set 𝓛 of 'lines' for his 1986 notes on 'réseaux via découpages'. The reading below of 𝓛 as pseudo-line-like objects is my interpretation and is not certain.

Data introduced on the previous page:
(a) A symmetric 'relative modular position' relation, given by a set S_0 of modular pairs. A finite subset T is modular if its elements are pairwise in modular position; Mod_f(𝓛) is the set of finite modular subsets.
(b) For each T in Mod_f(𝓛), the modular complement C(T) = {t ∉ T : T∪{t} modular}, together with an equivalence relation R_T on C(T). Its classes are called the 'connected components' of C(T).

This page adds:
(c) For each T in Mod_f(𝓛) and each component A in C(T)/R_T, a subset Ȧ ⊂ T, called the frontier of A.

These data are to satisfy axioms not yet stated. Grothendieck writes that he 'hoped' the axioms would imply two reductions:
1°) the frontier data (c) is already determined by (b);
2°) the component data (b) for every finite modular T is determined by the R_T for T in S_0 alone, i.e. for modular pairs.

Hence the only essential data would be:
- the modular relation on pairs (reflexive and symmetric);
- for each modular pair ε, the equivalence relation R_ε on C(ε).

This is a 'rank-2 data determines everything' programme. The structure would be generated by its pairwise (rank-2) local information, much as the global combinatorics of an arrangement is recovered from local two-element configurations.

He then begins 'Axiomes préliminaires' by naming the subsets of the form C(T) 'parties modulaires cofinies'. The next page uses this: if a part is both finite modular and cofinite modular, then 𝓛 is the discrete structure. In that case S_0 = P_2(𝓛), Mod_f = P_f(𝓛), C(T) = 𝓛∖T, R_T is discrete and every Ȧ is empty. This discrete structure is Example 1, the degenerate case.

The purpose is an axiomatic, purely combinatorial description of how a family of curves/lines cuts ('découpe') a space into components, with frontiers, as a foundation for 'réseaux'.
errors: No errors as such; the page states desiderata ('J'espérais que...'), not proved claims. Whether 1°) and 2°) follow depends on axioms not yet formulated. The past tense 'espérais' suggests he may already doubt that the reduction to pairs holds in general.

ideas.what: Abstract set of 'lines' with a pairwise modular-position relation, finite modular subsets, a modular complement C(T) with an equivalence relation into 'connected components', and a frontier Ȧ ⊂ T for each component
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial axiomatization of arrangements / chamber-type structures (cf. oriented matroids, pseudoline arrangements, chamber systems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroids: Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence (1970s); pseudoline arrangements: Levi, Goodman–Pollack; chamber systems: Tits
ideas.where_published: The 'réseaux'/'découpages' theme is related in spirit to the Esquisse d'un programme discussions of tame topology and maps; this specific formalism is not known to be published.

ideas.what: Hope that all the structure is determined by its restriction to modular pairs (rank 2): R_ε for ε ∈ S_0, plus the pairwise relation, with frontiers derived
ideas.modern_name: local-to-global / rank-2 determination (cf. chamber systems determined by rank-2 residues; arrangements determined by local sequences)

ideas.what: Definition of 'modular cofinite parts' as the subsets of the form C(T)

missed.claim: Programme of reducing an axiomatic 'network/cutting' structure to rank-2 data (modular pairs and their component relations), with frontier data derivable. Stated as a hope; the axioms that would realize it are not given on this page.
missed.quote: J'espérais que les axiomes impliquent ceci: 1°) que la donnée ⓒ résulte déjà de ⓑ 2°) que la donnée ⓑ résulte de la donnée des R_T, pour le cas particulier où T ∈ S_0.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of mild interest as a variant of known rank-2 determination phenomena for arrangements and chamber systems. Whether this particular formalism admits such a reduction is unclear, and is likely subsumed by oriented-matroid theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Setting up definitions plus a stated hope for rank-2 determination of an ad hoc combinatorial structure. The structure parallels known frameworks (oriented matroids, chamber systems), and nothing is proved on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'une partie de Ȧ ⊂ T' should read 'une partie Ȧ ⊂ T, appelée frontière de A'.
'Appelons les U de C [?] formes C(T) parties modulaires cofinies[?]' should read 'Appelons les U de la forme C(T) parties modulaires cofinies'.
'ⓐ celle des morphismes' is uncertain; it may read 'celle des modularités'. Context: the notion of relative modular position.
'{+réflexive et+} cocluse[?] [-syntaxiques-]' is more plausibly '(relation ... réflexive et symétrique)'.
The struck line '[-Soit Σ ∈ C(T), un pas-]' is largely illegible; Σ is uncertain.
